Karunanidhi]]. A Member of Parliament for 36 years, he was Union Minister in three separate central governments, and in charge of [[Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs|Urban Development]] in the [[V. P. Singh]] government; Industry in the [[H. D. Deve Gowda|Gowda]] and [[Inder Kumar Gujral|Gujral]] governments; and [[Ministry of Commerce and Industry (India)|Commerce and Industry]] under [[Atal Bihari Vajpayee|Vajpayee]].{{cite web |url= http://www.hinduonnet.com/fline/fl2025/stories/20031219003709700.htm |date=December 2003 |title= A man of many parts|author= T. Subramanian |work=Frontline Magazine |accessdate= 9 September 2006 |url-status= usurped |archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20070221042413/http://www.hinduonnet.com/fline/fl2025/stories/20031219003709700.htm |archivedate = 21 February 2007 |df = dmy-all}} Outside of politics, Maran was a journalist and scriptwriter for films.{{cite web|url=http://www.hinduonnet.com/2003/11/25/stories/2003112500951000.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070221043441/http://www.hinduonnet.com/2003/11/25/stories/2003112500951000.htm|url-status=usurped|archive-date=21 February 2007|title=MURASOLI MARAN, 1934–2003 |work=The Hindu tamil|date=25 November 2003|accessdate=9 September 2006}} ==Biography== Murasoli Maran was born on 17 August 1934 to Shanmugasundari, the elder sister of [[M. Karunanidhi]], in [[Thirukkuvalai]], [[Madras Presidency]] in present-day [[Tamil Nadu]]. After completing his basic education in his hometown, he moved to [[Madras]] to get an [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] from [[Pachaiyappa's College]] and [[Dr. Ambedkar Government Law College, Chennai|Madras Law College]]. While at school, he became involved with DMK. Before joining politics, he was an editor for the [[Tamil (language)|Tamil]] daily newspaper ''[[Murasoli (India)|Murasoli]]'' and the English weekly ''The Rising Sun''. He also worked on the Tamil-language publications ''[[Kungumam (magazine)|Kungumam]]'', ''Muththaram'', ''Vannathirai'' and ''Sumangali''. Maran later worked as a social worker.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}} He was vocal against [[Hindi (language)|Hindi]] being introduced in Tamil Nadu and was arrested during the [[Anti-Hindi agitations of Tamil Nadu#Agitation of 1965|Agitation of 1965]]. He was detained for a year under the [[Maintenance of Internal Security Act]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20030204203310/http://did.nic.in/improfile/profile.htm MR. MURASOLI MARAN. UNION MINISTER FOR COMMERCE & INDUSTRY GOVERNMENT OF INDIA NEW DELHI]. nic.in Maran was first elected to [[Lok Sabha]] in [[1967 Indian general election in Madras State|1967]], followed by a reelection in [[1971 Indian general election in Tamil Nadu|1971]]. He was a member of [[Rajya Sabha]] from 1977 to 1995, during which he was on the Committee on Public Undertakings for three terms. Other committees he took part in were the General Purposes Committee (1980–1982); the Public Accounts Committee (1980–1982, 1991-1995); the Committee on the Welfare of [[Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes]] (1982–1983, 1987-1988); and the Committee on Subordinate Legislation (1988–1989); the Joint Parliamentary Committee to enquire into irregularities in the securities and banking transactions (1992–1993). He also served as Union Cabinet Minister, first in [[Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs|Urban Development]] (1989-1990), then in [[Ministry of Commerce and Industry (India)|Industry]] (1996-1998, 1999-2002). He then returned to Lok Sabha in [[11th Lok Sabha|1996]], [[12th Lok Sabha|1998]], and [[13th Lok Sabha|1999]].{{citation needed|date=April 2025}} Prior to his death in November 2003, he was a Cabinet Minister [[Minister without portfolio#India|without portfolio]]. Maran married Mallika on 15 September 1963 he and they had two sons, [[Dayanidhi Maran|Dayanidhi]] and [[Kalanithi Maran|Kalanithi]], and one daughter, Anbukarasi. Dayanidhi Maran previously served as an MP and Union Minister and Kalanithi owns [[Sun TV (India)|Sun TV]]. Anbukarasi is a cardiologist.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}} Maran was admitted to [[Houston Methodist Hospital]] in the United States on 14 November 2002 with heart ([[hypertrophic cardiomyopathy]]) and kidney issues. He later received treatment at [[Apollo Hospital]] in [[Chennai]]. In late 2003, he fell into a coma, eventually dying aged 69 on 23 November 2003.[http://www.rediff.com/money/2003/nov/23maran.htm Murasoli Maran dies after prolonged illness]. Rediff.com (23 November 2003). Retrieved on 14 November 2018. He was a Minister without portfolio when he died, with his portfolio given to [[Arun Shourie]]. Then-Prime Minister [[Atal Bihari Vajpayee]] was among those who attended his funeral in Chennai.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}} He was survived by his mother, uncle, wife, children, children-in-law and grandchildren. ==Rajya Sabha Election History== {| class="wikitable sortable" !
